title: Disc replacement and second-title boot
symptom: Replacing a running PAL title with another PAL title could leave the old application active or repeatedly return to the player shell after Play.
expected: First insertion reaches an empty player through a live media-change event; replacing mounted media cold-boots the new disc once while preserving battery-backed saves.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: A reset or live media-change event retains volatile main, CDIC, or DVC state owned by the preceding application; replacement needs a cold player power boundary while NVRAM remains battery-backed.
supporting_evidence: The same saved PAL NVRAM boots the replacement correctly from a cold headless start.
PAL-to-PAL replacement failed while a player-standard change, which rebuilt more state, could boot.
Machine::power_cycle on replacement fixed the sequence without clearing the saved game.
contradicting_evidence: A clean-NVRAM replacement once succeeded without a cold power cycle, so stale volatile state is conditional.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Repeat PAL-to-PAL replacement with the previously looping NVRAM after a cold Machine::power_cycle; failure would show that retained volatile state is insufficient to explain the loop.

context.scenario: PAL title to Library to second PAL title to Play

experiments.strategy: Cold-power-cycle only replacement media while preserving NVRAM and keep first insertion as a live event.
assumptions: The saved PAL NVRAM is valid because it independently cold-boots the title.
The cyan player startup screen is expected after a deliberate cold replacement.
experiments.expected: The second PAL title boots after one Play request and a real save remains after application restart.
experiments.actual: The user confirmed both the replacement sequence and save persistence.
improvements: PAL-to-PAL replacement no longer loops at the player shell.
Battery-backed title storage survives replacement and application restart.

conditions: Replacing already-mounted media in the desktop frontend
invalidated_by: Changes to Machine power-cycle semantics, frontend disc-load policy, SLAVE media-change behavior, or NVRAM storage
repeat_when: Any of those dependencies changes or replacement behavior regresses

manual_verification.notes: PAL-to-PAL replacement boots the second title after Play; the cyan startup screen is expected for a cold replacement.
A newly created title save remained after quitting and relaunching E-Di.
